entries.proposition: SUBSTITUTE (NOT WWOX EVIDENCE). The defining readout of the disease, a low CSF 5-methyltetrahydrofolate, was NOT measured in either patient: the diagnosis rests on exome sequencing, so the report does not show what the CSF readout looks like in practice.
entries.snippet: Unfortunately, we could not measure the levels of CSF MTHF as the test is not present in our country.

experimental_context.system: two unrelated girls with intractable myoclonic-atonic epilepsy, Egypt; SUBSTITUTE, not WWOX evidence

entries.proposition: Case 1's variant is called nonsense and written c.C382T p.R128W; by the usual protein-change notation Arg-to-Trp is a missense substitution (INFERENCE from the notation, not looked up in a database), so either the label or the protein change is wrong. Case 2's p.Cys109Ter is a stop.
entries.snippet: revealing homozygous nonsense pathogenic variant in FOLR1 gene in exon 3 c.C382T p.R128W

experimental_context.system: two unrelated girls with intractable myoclonic-atonic epilepsy, Egypt; SUBSTITUTE, not WWOX evidence

entries.proposition: The routine metabolic work-up was NORMAL in the first patient, including blood ammonia, lactate, acylcarnitines, urine organic acids and CSF glucose, protein and lactate with a normal CSF-to-blood glucose ratio: a cerebral folate transport deficiency does not show on the standard metabolic screen listed in the review checklist, which is the class-level point.
entries.snippet: Laboratory investigations as blood ammonia, serum lactate, acyl carnitine profile in blood, and urine organic acid, were done with normal results.

experimental_context.system: two unrelated girls with intractable myoclonic-atonic epilepsy, Egypt; SUBSTITUTE, not WWOX evidence

entries.proposition: Treatment response is described without numbers: case 1 'better controlled (less frequent and less duration)' on 1 mg/kg/day intramuscular folinic acid; case 2 'partial reduction in the frequency of seizures' on 2 mg/kg/day; no seizure counts before and after, no EEG or CSF follow-up; the authors attribute incomplete control to late diagnosis.
entries.snippet: At this dose of folinic acid, seizures became better controlled (less frequent and less duration).

experimental_context.system: two unrelated girls with intractable myoclonic-atonic epilepsy, Egypt; SUBSTITUTE, not WWOX evidence

entries.proposition: Class-level caution stated in the Discussion: folic acid competes with folinic acid at the folate receptor and is contraindicated in this condition; a folate supplement is therefore not a neutral addition in a folate-transport disorder.
entries.snippet: Interestingly, folic acid is contraindicated in these conditions as it competitively binds to FRα, further reducing 5-MTHF transport into the brain.
